source.title: Input margins can predict generalization too
source.authors: Coenraad Mouton; Marthinus W. Theunissen; Marelie Hattingh Davel

page_placements.theme: Margins, norms and input sensitivity have conditional predictive value

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendix; no apparent corruption or truncation.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures input and hidden margins on trained networks and reports how they rank generalization, using a different margin measure from V7's magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.gate_note: The paper reports margin-to-test-accuracy correlations and CMI scores. These bear on the broader question of whether measured properties track generalization, but do not measure the magnitude-aware sharpness specified in V7. The paper does not test V1–V6 or V8.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates input and hidden margins as predictors of generalization. It does not measure magnitude-aware weight sharpness, compare sharpness against margins, or report results testing V1–V6 or V8. A different generalization predictor does not constitute a different method testing V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that restricting input-margin measurements to high-utility PCA subspaces improves generalization prediction and performs competitively against hidden margins and other PGDL predictors. They acknowledge task-dependent weaknesses, depth-related discrepancies, and sensitivity to principal-component selection.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops and evaluates a PCA-constrained input-margin measure on the PGDL benchmark; it does not reproduce the magnitude-aware sharpness measurement in V7.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance varies by task and hidden-layer selection. Constrained-margin performance also varies with principal-component count, clipping, and the choice of Taylor approximation versus DeepFool; the paper reports these in the appendix.

fits_no_version.finding: Across eight PGDL tasks, constrained input margins have mean Kendall correlation 0.6605 with test accuracy, versus 0.2392 for standard input margins. Performance varies by task and hidden-layer selection; first-layer hidden margins outperform constrained margins on Tasks 4 and 5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: PCA-constrained input margins can predict relative generalization among trained models, with task- and depth-dependent limitations.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed constrained-margin predictor obtains a held-out-task average CMI score of 27.03 and the highest reported score on four of eight tasks; comparison methods' scores in Table 2 come from prior publications.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: PCA-constrained input margins provide competitive generalization prediction on PGDL, without consistently outperforming alternative predictors.

record.problems: The study uses aggregate rank correlations and CMI over task model sets, with no uncertainty estimates reported in the supplied text. Performance is task-dependent; the authors note depth-related discrepancies and weaker performance for some tasks. The measure is predictive association, not evidence of a causal relationship.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the selected main comparison tables. The appendix also reports additional margin-method, component-count, sample-count, and clipping analyses; those were not separately extracted here because the rows focus on the main reported comparisons.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the paired natural-label versus random-label held-out performance comparison.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Controlled comparisons of convolutional and fully connected classifiers, including local connectivity and initialization effects.
Held-out performance comparisons between adaptive optimizers and SGD under specified tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover held-out performance.
Effects of adding or removing dropout, including dataset-size and augmentation interactions.

Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking relative to norm- and margin-based measures. Input-space and hidden-representation margins are different quantities.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All extracted numerical values match the supplied tables. No listed version receives a verdict. Appendix analyses are declared in rows_left_out and do not add a test of any listed version. The supplied manuscript identifies itself as a preprint under review; it does not substantiate the record's AAAI publication attribution.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Dropout and its interaction with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
The study tests input and hidden margin correlations, not magnitude-aware sharpness or its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.
